items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: then with Rosetta and Marie I made "Precious Memories."

ctx.x: Somebody asked me, though, over at the West End the other night, asked me to tell him the ten best records, you know, that I've made during my career. And I told him that I like "I'm Coming, Virginia" by Henry Red Allen...I place that number one, and number two was "Back Home" with Sidney Bechet, and number three was "Up Above My Head" with Rosetta Tharpe and "I Cover the Waterfront" with Doc Cheatham. And then "The Freight Train Blues" with Trixie Smith and Sidney Bechet. And then I wrote a tune back in fifties,…
Then I recorded Ida Cox's "Death Letter Blues," and then with Rosetta and Marie I made "Precious Memories." And then the next best thing that I thought I like was Doc Cheatham

playing "What Can I Say Dear After I Say I'm Sorry." And then last was that "Manhattan Blues" that I made with Jonah Jones. That was the...oh, Jonah was on that record date that I made with Vic and those guys on Jazztone. So those were the ten best records, you know what I mean, as far as I was concerned.
